what_its_for: Epinastine eye drops are used to relieve itchy eyes caused by allergies (also called allergic conjunctivitis). It works by blocking histamine, the chemical your body releases during an allergic reaction, to reduce itching and redness in your eyes.
how_to_take: Wash your hands before using these eye drops. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and place one drop into the pocket. Gently close your eye for 1 to 2 minutes. Try not to blink or squeeze your eye too hard. Do not touch the tip of the dropper bottle to your eye, fingers, or any surface to keep it clean and germ-free. If you wear soft contact lenses, remove them before putting in the drops and wait at least 10 minutes before putting your contacts back in.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children 3 years and older is ONE drop in each affected eye TWICE a day (about every 12 hours, such as morning and evening). Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not use more drops than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use the missed drop as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your normal schedule. Do not double up by using two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medication at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze the eye drops. Throw away the bottle 28 days after opening, even if there is still medicine left in it, unless your pharmacist or doctor tells you otherwise.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching the tip of the dropper to any surface, including your eyes or hands, to prevent contamination and infection. Do not wear soft contact lenses while your eyes are red or irritated. Avoid rubbing your eyes after using the drops. These drops are for use in the eyes only — do not swallow them or use them in any other way.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor if you notice: increased eye redness, swelling, or worsening eye irritation after using the drops; eye pain that does not go away; vision changes or blurry vision that persists; signs of an eye infection such as discharge, crusting, or significant redness; or an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Seek emergency help right away if you have severe trouble breathing or swallowing.
when_it_works: Epinastine starts working quickly — you may feel relief from eye itching within a few minutes of using the drops. The full effect usually lasts up to 8 to 12 hours. It works best when used regularly as directed, especially during allergy season.
special_populations: Children: This medication is approved for children 3 years of age and older at the same adult dose. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this medication. It is not fully known whether epinastine passes into breast milk, so discuss the risks and benefits with your healthcare provider. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is typically needed for older adults, but always follow your doctor's instructions.
